newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Aug 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Qantas Airways will invite tenders for virtually all aspects of its ground operations at the Kingsford Smith, Cairns, Townsville, and Coolangatta airports as it continues the push to reduce costs. This is the most significant step so far in the airline's progressive introduction of competitive tendering. Page 1.

Investors in non-bank mortgage providers such as Aussie Home Loans and RAMS Mortgage Corp are forcing their financiers to pay higher yields, and reducing their exposure to mortgage-backed bonds, putting pressure on the ability of the mortgage managers to compete with banks. Page 1.

Industrial Equity Ltd will make its last major sell-off from the former Adelaide Steamship group of companies by putting up for tender its 55.7 per cent majority stake in property developer and brickmaker Norwest Ltd. IEL is expected to make a net profit of A$40 million on the sale. Page 19.

BHP Diamonds president and group general manager Jim Rothwell said last week no plans had been finalised to market diamonds from the company's Lac de Gras project in Canada. He said options included selling some of the product through the De Beers-controlled Central Selling Organisation, some through joint ventures with other companies, and others through BHP's new Antwerp marketing office. Page 19.

Federal Finance Minister John Fahey announced the last appointment of co-lead managers and co-managers to the partial float of Telstra on Friday, bringing to a close a six-month selection process. Seventeen stockbroking firms were chosen from 30 competitors to make up the third tier of brokers handling Telstra's A$10 billion public offering. Page 20.

Newly appointed Davids Ltd chief executive Don Bourke says the problems with the company can be fixed, that it is not going to collapse, and that Woolworths did not cause its current problems. Davids intends to upgrade 33 company-owned stores and exit 32 others as part of a rationalisation announced last week. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

National Australia Bank chief executive Don Argus has emphasised the necessity of developing fee income from account fees and new sources including funds management and custodial and trustee services, as the Bank faces falling profits from interest and an assault on their non-traditional revenues. Page 29.

FoodWorks Food Today chairman Jack Scanlon said yesterday the new group had signed more than 30 stores in the past fortnight, representing more than A$200 million in sales, in what is believed to be a poaching of the Tuckerbag chain of stores which was previously supplied by troubled wholesale group Davids'. Page 29.

The June Quarter edition of Access Economics' Five Year Business Outlook has revealed interest rates will rise early next year as a result of a pickup in the Australian economy, a rise in inflation and a credit squeeze by Australia's international lenders. Page 29.

North Star BHP president Edward Fox said last Friday the company's joint venture Delta steel project in the United States would reach its capacity output of 1.5 million tonnes a year by July 1998, and by October of that year BHP and Delta partner Cargill ould look at investing an extra one million tonnes of capacity. Page 29.

The Australian Taxation Office is undertaking to halve the number of pages in the Capital Gains Tax Act to 150 pages as part of the Tax Law Improvement Project's last stage. The final changes are aimed at putting the CGT laws into an easy-to-use format for small business owners and operators. Page 33.

Queensland's Cloncurry mining area is at the heart of a revival with Eagle Mining Corp NL about to begin drilling for gold in the Wallace South prospect. The area, licensed by Cloncurry Mining Co NL, was once targeted for oxide copper but has now been identified as largely a gold discovery. Page 34.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The AMP Society board will meet later this month to approve an explanatory document which will be sent to more than two million policy holders in September to vote on the demutualisation of the company. The company's plans have won the support of independent expert KPMG, and would see it become one of the nation's biggest listed companies. Page 41.

Stockbroking analysts have adjusted down their profit forecasts for News Corp, which Rupert Murdoch said would lift its profits by 20 per cent in the year to June 1997, following the poor box office performance of the Fox movie Speed 2: Cruise Control, which is expected to record a loss of between A$40 million and A$100 million. Page 41.

The New South Wales TAB board will tomorrow consider a recommendation on the preferred bidder for the 15-year rights to operate the organisation's planned State-wide linked jackpot system and gaming machine monitoring licence. Front-runners are believed to be AWA and IGDreamport. Page 41.

E.C. Consolidated Capital director Anthony Senese yesterday gave an undertaking to the Australian Securities Commission he would not try to leave the country, after the ASC took legal action in relation to an investigation trying to locate former ECCC key executive Tim Gatland, A$10 million of superannuation money invested in ECCC, and A$39 million in missing Thai bearer bonds. Page 41.

De Beers Central Selling Organisation is pushing for control of the marketing of the output of BHP and its partners' North-West Territories diamond mine in Canada. North-West project manager Jim Rothwell says the mine's partners will explore a range of options ranging from selling entirely through CSO to selling it wholly alone. Page 41.

Sydney-based gold miner Plutonic Resources said it would maintain profitability, despite falling gold prices, due to its low-cost Centenary and Plutonic mines. Plutonic general manager corporate Denis Clarke said the company expected 600,000 ounces to be produced from the two mines by 2000. Page 43.
THE AGE

Diners Club's Grant Halverson and American Express' John Schaap say they are both preparing to use their cards to compete with transaction banking through the EFTPOS network, but will require exchange settlement accounts with the Reserve Bank, which are not currently available to non-banks, though Treasurer Peter Costello is considering the issue as part of his response to the Wallis report. Page B1.

Independent expert KPMG has lent its support to the AMP Society's plans to demutualise, with a meeting of the board scheduled for later this month to approve an explanatory document for policy voters who will be asked to vote "yes" at the company's demutualisation meeting on 20 November. Page B1.

Adelaide-based pharmaceuticals company F.H. Faulding's executives cannot explain why the company has failed to attract investors despite a series of acquisitions, international drug approvals, an upcoming rights issue, a new pharmacy franchising scheme, and footholds in diverse international markets. Page B1.

The Australian Telecommunications Industry Association, which represents the manufacturers of telecommunications equipment, will boycott an Industry Commission inquiry, claiming the Commission is biased and lacks the skills to conduct the inquiry. Page B3

News Corporation is being tipped to make a profit just under A$1.5 billion for the year to June 1997, down on Rupert Murdoch's predicted 20 per cent increase in profits, following an loss of up to A$100 million from the Fox movie Speed 2: Cruise Control. page B3.

Independent retail chain Foodworks Food Today chairman Jack Scanlon said the group of more than 30 stores had switched from troubled grocery wholesaler Davids to rival supplier Woolworths in order to ensure the Victorian chain's survival. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
